thread:
kai: Quick follow-up on the iterator/resume RFC — I'm proposing a lightweight PaginatorV2 that returns an opaque resume_token on each page. Goal: language-parity across py/ts/go, explicit resume API, and clear transport semantics for streaming vs polling. Looking for tradeoffs + surface suggestions.

lucy: Do you mean every page includes the token and a TTL? how do we handle token invalidation when we roll a new model or change ordering?

kai: Yes, include token + TTL. Server should include x-resume-ttl header. If model/ordering changes invalidate token, server should return 410 with a recommended new_token or a hint to restart. We want SDKs to surface that to callers.

omar: Transport note: streaming vs polling will differ. For streaming we can have a resume-id header and resume from last acked sequence. For polling it's just ?cursor=token. Question: should SDK hide transport differences or expose resume semantics explicitly? I'm leaning toward hiding it and exposing a single Resume() on the paginator.

sasha: SDK ergonomics: Python async iterator should yield Page objects with .resume_token and provide paginator.resume(token) to get a new iterator. In TS an AsyncGenerator that returns an object with resumeToken seems natural, but resuming an AsyncGenerator is awkward.

matt: Go needs explicit control: pattern like: type Paginator interface { Next(ctx) (Page, error); Resume(ctx, token) error } and Next must be safe to call after Resume. Also ensure Next respects ctx cancellation.

rachel: On retries & idempotency: if a resume triggers a server-side retry that can replay partial page, we need strong idempotency semantics. For read-only lists it's ok, but any operation that might mutate should require client-supplied idempotency-key. For resume we should accept server-stable sequence ids.

lucy: Edge-case: partial-page resume vs page-level resume. If network drops mid-page, do we resume at item offset? That complicates token. Alternative: commit only at page boundaries and encourage smaller pages.

kai: Tradeoffs noted. I'm proposing two modes: granularity='page' (cheap, server keeps checkpoint per-page) and granularity='item' (finer resume but larger server state + token complexity). Default to 'page'.

omar: Performance tradeoff: item-granularity is better for flaky mobile networks but adds complexity. Maybe support both via PaginatorV2Options.

sasha: API suggestion (TS/Py): PaginatorV2Options = { granularity: 'page'|'item', auto_resume: boolean, retry_policy: { max_attempts, backoff_ms, respect_retry_after } } and expose per-page metadata: { resume_token, retry_after, request_id }. Example Python usage:

```python
async for page in client.list_items_paginator(page_size=100, options=PaginatorV2Options(...)):
    process(page.items)
    if page.resume_token:
        save_checkpoint(page.resume_token)
```

matt: For Go, add ResumeFrom(token) which returns a new Paginator instance so callers can ensure deterministic lifecycle and defer close.

rachel: Also require servers to honor Retry-After semantics. SDK should respect 429/503 Retry-After and surface when a resume token has expired. Add built-in fallbacks: if 410 received, emit specific error type ResumeExpiredError.

kai: Agreed. Default retry policy: conservative — 2 retries for 5xx, respect Retry-After. Add opt-in aggressive policy for high-throughput backends.

lucy: About semver: any change to token format must be forward/backward compatible. Treat token as opaque, never decode in SDK. Server side may add new internal fields but keep decode tolerant.

omar: Ops concern: server retention window for resume tokens -> storage implications. We'll need a TTL configurable per-tenant and metrics on resume hit rate.

sasha: UX concern: how do we document best practices? e.g., prefer page-granularity, smaller pages for mobile, save resume token after processing page. Add snippet to SDK docs.

kai: Next steps: I'll draft the RFC delta covering token semantics, transport headers (x-resume-ttl, x-resume-id, x-resume-offset), and SDK sketches for py/ts/go. Can folks +1 or add blockers here?

rachel: +1. Also add a test checklist for flaky resume cases.

ci-bot: Build failed on branch resume-paginator-proto — flaky test TestResumePartialPage in go/paginator_test.go (0.2% flake). Rerun started.

kai: Thanks — I'll start the draft and tag eng-runtime + infra for storage/ops input.

lucy: small nit: add example of server response for expired token: `HTTP/1.1 410 Gone` with body `{"error":"resume_token_expired","new_cursor_hint":null}` — SDK should map to ResumeExpiredError.

omar: Also note metrics: resume.success, resume.expired, resume.invalid, resume.retry_count.

kai: Great — I'll include metrics and TTL config in the RFC. Planning to circulate by EOD for sprint planning.
